statement: Upon the registration of a charitable incorporated organisation in the register of charities, it becomes by virtue of the registration a body corporate whose constitution is that proposed in the application, whose name is that specified in the constitution, and whose first member is, or first members are, the applicants referred to in section 207.
caveat: Property held by the applicants on trust for the CIO's charitable purposes vests in the CIO on registration (section 210(2)). The application contents and the Commission's refusal grounds are in sections 207 to 209. Until registration the CIO does not exist, so it cannot contract or hold property itself.
